**NEITHER!** By Newton's Second Law (F = m * a) and the Impulse-Momentum Theorem (F * dt = m * dv), a 12,000 kg spacecraft has 100% of its Earth mass and inertia (m = 12,000 kg), regardless of whether we're on the Moon (0.165 g), Mars (0.379 g), or floating in deep space (0 g). Stopping a given velocity requires the EXACT SAME 1.0x braking impulse (m * dv) as on Earth—never less and never 100x more! On the Moon, downward weight (W = m * g) is reduced to 16.5% (16.2 m of lift to counter 100 kg of mass), but floating in vacuum means 100% of your braking impulse must still push against 100% of your mass.

At the equator, high daytime solar irradiance and hot surrounding regolith raise the effective thermal sink temperature, requiring ~216.2 m2 of radiator area to reject waste heat at the cold Lunar Pole sink (133.4 m2). Per NTRS 20040015099, cooling requires C * L_C mass, where L_C is the thermal cooling mass factor (kg heat rejected / m2 radiator area per kW of reactor power). Higher radiator area reduces thermal load per m2, cutting cooling mass!
